activities.instructions: Desliza a la derecha si la frase es correcta y a la izquierda si no lo es.
activities.prompt: Mazo de 7 afirmaciones para repasar el tema.

cards.statement: A cough is a kind of furniture.
cards.explanation: A cough is a symptom involving a repeated sound or action.

cards.statement: If you feel dizzy, you may feel that you are losing your balance.
cards.explanation: Dizzy describes a feeling of spinning or poor balance.

cards.statement: Get some rest is a general piece of health advice.
cards.explanation: Get some rest is a common general recommendation for mild tiredness or illness.

cards.statement: A headache is pain in the head.
cards.explanation: Headache is the standard word for pain in the head.

cards.statement: A headache is the same thing as a sore throat.
cards.explanation: A headache affects the head; a sore throat affects the throat.

cards.statement: A fever is an unusually low body temperature.
cards.explanation: A fever is an unusually high body temperature.

cards.statement: A bruise can be a dark mark after an impact.
cards.explanation: A bruise is caused by bleeding under the skin after an impact or pressure.

activities.instructions: Desliza a la derecha si la frase es correcta y a la izquierda si no lo es.
activities.prompt: Mazo de 8 afirmaciones para repasar el tema.

cards.statement: Swollen describes a body part that has become larger.
cards.explanation: Swollen often results from inflammation or injury.

cards.statement: Vocabulary about symptoms should always be used to diagnose yourself.
cards.explanation: The vocabulary helps describe symptoms and ask for help; diagnosis should be left to a qualified professional.

cards.statement: A pharmacist and a doctor have exactly the same role.
cards.explanation: Both can help with health, but doctors examine and diagnose while pharmacists focus on medicines and pharmacy advice.

cards.statement: A bandage is used to cover and protect a small wound.
cards.explanation: A bandage covers and protects a cut or wound.

cards.statement: A bruise is usually an injury to a joint caused by twisting it.
cards.explanation: A sprain affects a joint after twisting; a bruise is a dark mark after an impact.

cards.statement: Make an appointment means arrange a time to see a professional.
cards.explanation: An appointment is an arranged meeting, often with a doctor or dentist.

cards.statement: The standard expression is allergic with pollen.
cards.explanation: The standard expression is allergic to pollen.

cards.statement: If pain lasts several days, asking a doctor for advice may be sensible.
cards.explanation: Persistent symptoms may need professional assessment; the sentence does not attempt a diagnosis.

cards.statement: A pharmacist is the person who rents out your flat.
cards.explanation: A pharmacist works with medicines; a landlord rents out a flat.

cards.statement: A sore throat and a stomach ache refer to different parts of the body.
cards.explanation: The throat and stomach are different body areas.

cards.statement: The phrase make an appointment is natural English.
cards.explanation: Make an appointment is the standard collocation.

cards.statement: A person can feel dizzy without having a fever.
cards.explanation: Dizziness and fever are different symptoms and do not always occur together.

cards.statement: You can say My knee hurts to describe pain in the knee.
cards.explanation: Hurt can follow the body part directly.
